title: fix(cli,driver-turso): os migrate plan on a Turso remote database lists the changes it cannot apply with the transport's limit, not --allow-destructive
body:
Fixes #23925

Clause-②: yes (widening)

## What changes

On a Turso REMOTE primary (`libsql://...`), neither `os migrate plan` nor `os migrate apply` (its listing before the prompt, and both of its held-back lines) offers `--allow-destructive` for a drift entry that database cannot apply. The driver that reported each entry declares what its apply door cannot perform, and both commands read that declaration. Neither branches on the dialect, the transport name, the URL or the driver's class.

- **The declaration (driver-turso).** `REMOTE_DRIFT_OP_ANSWERS` in `turso-driver.ts` answers every drift op the shared differ emits with `applied`, `needs-table-rebuild` or `report-only`. Its `satisfies Record(DriftOp type, answer)` clause fails the package's typecheck when an op is added to `DriftOp` and left unclassified, the `REMOTE_FACE_ANSWERS` pattern. The REMOTE `applyMigrationEntries` dispatches by it: only `applied` rows are sent, and every other entry is skipped before any DDL and logged with its reason. `TursoDriver.driftApplyLimit(opType)` answers from the same rows: the limit sentence for a `needs-table-rebuild` op, `null` for every other op, and `null` for every op on the local and embedded-replica faces. The commands and the apply door therefore read one object and cannot disagree about an entry.
- **The seam (cli, `schema-migrate.ts`).**
  - `SchemaStack.driftApplyLimit(entry)` asks the driver that reported the entry. That is the `driftOwners` map `applyMigrationEntries` already routes by, read through the optional `SqlDriverLike.driftApplyLimit`. A driver that declares nothing has no limit.
  - `collectDriftApplyLimits(stack, drift)` gathers the entries that have a limit.
  - `describeWithApplyLimits(limits)` is the one spelling of the line printed under such an entry: its finding, then `"os migrate apply" cannot apply it on this database: LIMIT.`, in place of the `--allow-destructive` sentence. Both commands read it.
- **`os migrate plan`.** An entry with a limit is still listed and counted (it is still drift), under that line. The footer offers `--allow-destructive` only for the destructive entries the database can apply, drops the apply line when it can apply nothing listed, and says how many listed changes remain drift.
- **`os migrate apply`: its listing and its two held-back lines.**
  - The listing before the prompt passes `renderPlan` the same `describe`.
  - The count before the prompt, `N destructive change(s) will be SKIPPED (re-run with --allow-destructive to include them).`, now counts only the destructive entries a re-run could apply. The rest get their own line: `N destructive change(s) remain drift that a re-run with --allow-destructive cannot apply on this database either (each says why above).`
  - The line after the run splits the held-back entries by the same limits map: `Skipped N destructive change(s) (re-run with --allow-destructive to include them).` for those a re-run could apply, and `Skipped N destructive change(s) that a re-run could not apply on this database either: they remain drift (each says why above).` for the rest.
  - Nothing else changes: not `notApplied`, not PARTIAL, not the exit code, and not the `--json` document.
- **The remedy sentence (driver-sql).** `tighten_not_null`, `narrow_varchar` and `drop_column` messages end with an `os migrate apply --allow-destructive` sentence. That sentence is now spelled once (`DESTRUCTIVE_COLUMN_REMEDY`), with the same bytes. `driftFindingWithoutRemedy(entry)` takes exactly that tail off, and only the limited entries use it. Every other reader keeps the message as written.
- **Public surface: the widening the declaration line names.** `TursoDriver.driftApplyLimit` (`@objectstack/driver-turso`) and `driftFindingWithoutRemedy` (the `@objectstack/driver-sql` entry) are new and additive, so those two packages go `minor`. `@objectstack/cli` stays `patch`. No `packages/spec` contract and no accept set moves.
- **The CLI docs (`content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`).** One caveat under the migrate category table:

  > On a Turso remote primary (`libsql://`), a tightened or relaxed `NOT NULL` and a dropped DEFAULT stay drift, because that transport runs no SQLite table rebuild. `os migrate plan` and `os migrate apply` list each such entry with `"os migrate apply" cannot apply it on this database: it needs the SQLite table rebuild, which the Turso REMOTE transport does not run.`, offer `--allow-destructive` only for the destructive changes that database can apply, and count the rest as drift a re-run cannot apply.
- **No declaration, no change.** When no entry has a limit, both commands take the old code path: the same `renderPlan(drift)` call, the same footer string and the same held-back lines. That is every database but a Turso REMOTE one.

### Each drift op, and what the REMOTE face does with it

| op | category | emitted by the SQLite differ | REMOTE apply door |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `drop_column` | destructive | yes | applied |
| `drop_index` | destructive | yes | applied |
| `create_index` | safe | yes | applied |
| `recreate_index` | needs_confirm, or destructive when unique | yes | applied |
| `replace_unique_index` | safe | yes | applied |
| `relax_not_null` | needs_confirm | yes | skipped: needs the table rebuild |
| `tighten_not_null` | destructive | yes | skipped: needs the table rebuild |
| `drop_column_default` | safe | yes | skipped: needs the table rebuild |
| `widen_varchar` | safe | no (PostgreSQL / MySQL only) | skipped: needs the table rebuild |
| `narrow_varchar` | destructive | no (PostgreSQL / MySQL only) | skipped: needs the table rebuild |
| `manual_column_type_change` | needs_confirm | no (PostgreSQL / MySQL only) | report only, as on every face |
| `manual_widen_varchar_to_text` | needs_confirm | no (PostgreSQL / MySQL only) | report only, as on every face |
| `unbuildable_index` | needs_confirm | yes | report only, as on every face |

A report-only op answers `null` from `driftApplyLimit`. No face applies it, so its skip is not a limit of this transport, and its finding already names its remedy. The declaration is therefore a per-op answer rather than a set of appliable ops: a plain set would print this transport's rebuild reason against an `unbuildable_index`.

### Who reads the entry's `message`, and why each one stays truthful

The message keeps its bytes on every face. `schema-drift.remedy-sentence.test.ts` pins the three destructive column messages character for character. The report stays identical across faces, so `turso-remote-drift-detection.test.ts` keeps holding the local and remote reports equal. Only the human listings change what they print, and only for an entry whose driver declares a limit.

- `os migrate plan` (human, `renderPlan`): changed as above.
- `os migrate apply` (human, the listing before the prompt and the two held-back lines): changed as above.
- `os migrate plan --json` and `os migrate apply --json`: unchanged (acceptance note 1).
- The boot `[schema-drift]` warning (`SqlDriver.reconcileAndWarnDrift`): runs only on the Knex faces, where the apply door does rebuild, so its remedy is true.
- The `OS_ARTIFACT_URL` boot gate (`artifact-boot-migration.ts`): returns on the REMOTE face's `driftReportCaveat` before it reads a message.
- `REMOTE_DRIFT_REPORT_CAVEAT`: re-read, and still true ("applies those and names the rest as not applied"). Untouched.
- The organization-ownership ceremony (`messageOf`): reads messages only for its own column drops, which the REMOTE face applies. Its remote pin is green.

## Verification

All of it runs against a real `sqld` (libsql-server 0.24.32, `libsql://127.0.0.1:PORT?tls=0`, archive sha256 checked). The fixture is `apply.remote-face.integration.test.ts`'s own: a hand-made `os23848_note` table with three drifts, `legacy_23848` (`drop_column`), `code` (`tighten_not_null`) and `memo` (`relax_not_null`). Each remote case has a local SQLite file CONTROL. CI has no `sqld`, so the unit pins hold the same rules against a stubbed stack whose driver double carries the declaration: `plan.apply-limit.test.ts` and the new block in `apply.remote-posture.test.ts`.

### Red, then green: the plan

- **Red at `a512b914f`.** That commit holds the pins alone; its production code equals the base `2e1562091`.
  - sqld: 1 failed, 6 passed. The failure is the remote plan case, with `Received: "os23848_note.code: metadata declares ... must be backfilled. Run "os migrate apply --allow-destructive"."`. The local-file CONTROL is green.
  - Unit: 2 failed, 2 passed. The CONTROL and the `--json` case are green.
- **Green at `d99ee347e`.** sqld 7 of 7, unit 4 of 4.

### Red, then green: the apply's listing

- **Red at `ca87de9ee`.** That commit holds the pins alone; its production code equals `59f489f6d`.
  - sqld: 2 failed, 7 passed. The failures are the remote `apply --yes` listing case and the listing assertion in the remote `apply --allow-destructive` human case, both receiving `... must be backfilled. Run "os migrate apply --allow-destructive".`. Both local-file CONTROLs are green: `apply --yes` on a file keeps the remedy and `2 destructive change(s) will be SKIPPED (re-run ...)`.
  - Unit (`apply.remote-posture.test.ts`): 2 failed, 10 passed. The CONTROL and the `--json` equality case are green.
- **Green at `48ac51325`.**
  - sqld: 9 of 9, plus `organization-ownership.remote-face.integration.test.ts` 1 of 1 and `artifact-boot-migration.unbuildable-index.test.ts` 3 of 3.
  - Unit: 4 files, 28 tests.
  - The new `--json` pin compares the apply's document under a declaring driver with the one a driver that declares nothing gets, key for key and entry for entry.

### Red, then green: the apply's post-apply held-back line

- **Red at `db6056e76`.** That commit holds the pins alone; its production code equals `455c7f288`.
  - Unit (`apply.remote-posture.test.ts`): 1 failed, 11 passed. The failure is the limited case: it received `["  ⚠ Skipped 2 destructive change(s) (re-run with --allow-destructive to include them)."]` where two lines were expected. The CONTROL (`Skipped 2 ...`, unchanged) is green.
  - sqld: 1 failed, 8 passed. The failure is the remote `apply --yes` case, with the same received line. The local-file CONTROL (`Skipped 2 ...`) is green.
- **Green at `512414eef`.**
  - Unit: 4 files, 23 tests (`apply.remote-posture`, `apply.account-issuer-json-refusal`, `plan.apply-limit`, `schema-migrate.lazy-driver-import`).
  - sqld: `apply.remote-face.integration.test.ts` 9 of 9 and `organization-ownership.remote-face.integration.test.ts` 1 of 1.

### A pass for the wrong reason, closed

`apply.account-issuer-json-refusal.test.ts` stubs the stack without the new `driftApplyLimit` member. Its human case ("the human face of the same refusal exits 1") therefore still exited 1, but from a TypeError in the listing, before the pre-flight ran. The stub now declares no limit, and the case asserts the pre-flight ran.

### Ablations

- **The driver pin can fail.** At `d99ee347e`, `tighten_not_null` was changed from `'needs-table-rebuild'` to `'applied'` in `REMOTE_DRIFT_OP_ANSWERS`.
  - The mutation went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in WRAP mode, inside a script with a `trap` restore, and was proven on disk: anchor 1 to 0, blob `1a3a5461` to `37038760`.
  - `turso-remote-drift-apply-limit.test.ts` failed 1 and passed 3.
  - The file was restored to the HEAD blob, with `git diff HEAD` empty.
- **The issuer pin's new assertion can fail.** At `455c7f288`, the stub's `driftApplyLimit: () => null,` was deleted the same way: anchor 1 to 0, blob `fcd562cd` to `7509aeb0`.
  - The human case went red with `expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times`: 1 failed, 3 passed.
  - The file was restored to the HEAD blob, with `git diff HEAD` empty.
- **No build.** Both subjects resolve to `src/` through relative imports.

### End to end through the CLI's own entry

Both runs went through `tsx bin/run-dev.js`, on a `sqld` this run started and stopped by its PID, with the same three drifts on `os23925_note`. `migrate apply --yes` at `512414eef` exited 0, and read:

```text
  Destructive (requires --allow-destructive)
    ✗ os23925_note.code [tighten_not_null]
        os23925_note.code: metadata declares `storage.notNull` but the column is nullable — existing nulls must be backfilled. "os migrate apply" cannot apply it on this database: it needs the SQLite table rebuild, which the Turso REMOTE transport does not run.
    ✗ os23925_note.legacy_23925 [drop_column]
        os23925_note.legacy_23925: column exists in the database but not in metadata (orphaned) — "os migrate apply --allow-destructive" to drop it.
  ℹ 3 change(s): 0 safe, 1 needs-confirm, 2 destructive
  ⚠ 1 destructive change(s) will be SKIPPED (re-run with --allow-destructive to include them).
  ⚠ 1 destructive change(s) remain drift that a re-run with --allow-destructive cannot apply on this database either (each says why above).
  ✓ Applied 0 change(s).
  ⚠ Skipped 1 destructive change(s) (re-run with --allow-destructive to include them).
  ⚠ Skipped 1 destructive change(s) that a re-run could not apply on this database either: they remain drift (each says why above).
  ⚠ 1 change(s) were NOT applied — the driver could not perform them on this database (its log above says why), so the schema still differs from metadata there:
      • os23925_note.memo — relax_not_null
```

`migrate plan` at `d99ee347e` exited 0, and its footer read:

```text
  Apply with: os migrate apply (add --allow-destructive for the 1 destructive change(s) it can apply on this database)
  ⚠ 2 change(s) above cannot be applied on this database by "os migrate apply" (each says why), so they remain drift after it runs.
```

  - `--ran` reconciliation: 99 derived, 97 run with exit 0, 2 NOT MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.
  - The two NOT MEASURED are `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (packages outside this build closure have no `dist/`) and `check:i18n-coverage` (a partial round). Both exited 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET.

  - `check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base origin/main` exits 0 with no event, and exits 0 with an event carrying this body. With this body it reads `LEVEL AXIS: this PR declares clause-② yes (widening) ... at minor or above`, naming `@objectstack/driver-sql: minor` and `@objectstack/driver-turso: minor`, with `@objectstack/cli: patch` not refused.

  - 34 success, including `Build Docs` and four of the five required contexts (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Build Core` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard`).

## File surface

The claim's surface, and its amendments 6222387090, 6223299622 and 6223389541:

- `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/apply.ts`: only the listing before the prompt and the held-back count line (amendment 6222387090).
- `packages/cli/src/utils/schema-migrate.ts`: the `driftApplyLimit` seam, the two shared helpers, and an optional `describe` argument to `renderPlan`.
- `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/index.ts`: one re-export line.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/apply.ts`, by amendment 2 (6223299622): the post-apply held-back line as well.
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`, by amendment 3 (6223389541): one caveat under the migrate category table, and nothing else on the page.
- Tests beside each:
  - `plan.apply-limit.test.ts`;
  - `apply.remote-posture.test.ts`, whose stub stack gains the member, plus a new block;
  - `apply.account-issuer-json-refusal.test.ts`, whose stub gains the member, plus one assertion;
  - `apply.remote-face.integration.test.ts`, which holds the sqld fixture;
  - `schema-drift.remedy-sentence.test.ts`;
  - `turso-remote-drift-apply-limit.test.ts`.

Nothing under `packages/spec/**`, and no published driver contract (`packages/spec/src/contracts/**`) gains a member. Neither command reads `dialect`, the transport, the URL or a class name.

## Acceptance notes

1. **The `--json` documents are unchanged.** In `os migrate plan --json`, `changes[].message` keeps the shared remedy, and no field marks an entry the database cannot apply. `os migrate apply --json` is pinned equal to what a driver that declares nothing produces. Adding a mark widens a document, and no consumer of either JSON document was measured to need one.
2. **`drop_column_default`.** Its message carries `run "os migrate apply"` mid-sentence rather than as a tail. On a remote primary, the listing line therefore shows that sentence with the limit after it. That entry needs a literal runtime-token DEFAULT written by an old build, so a database the current sync created does not reach it.
3. **The REMOTE apply door's log.** A skipped rebuild entry now reads `... skipped: it needs the SQLite table rebuild, which the Turso REMOTE transport does not run`, from the declaration's sentence. It used to end `which this transport does not run`. A report-only `unbuildable_index` on that face is now logged as skipped; it used to be skipped with no log line. No test pins either log line.
